items.title: $25,000, grant to Dr. Mihaela-Rita Mihailescu and Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck
items.excerpt: Dr. Mihaela-Rita Mihailescu and Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck, Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, School of Science and Engineering, $25,000, from the Charles Henry Leach II Fund for Duquesne University to support the project Structure-Function in Alphaviruses Genome's Highly Conserved RNA Structures: New Therapeutic Targets

items.title: $507,121, grant to Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck
items.excerpt: Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck, Department of Chemistry, School of Science and Engineering, $507,121, from the National Institutes of Health to support the project RNA homodimerization strand displacement pathways to extended duplexes: Atomistic details for a mechanistic paradigm to identify unique antiviral targets for current and emerging viral pandemics.

items.title: $6,000, grant to Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck
items.excerpt: Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck, Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, School of Science and Engineering, $6,000, from Gaussian, Inc., to be used for the Center for Computational Sciences.

items.title: Evanseck Receives Presidential Award for Excellence in Research
items.excerpt: Dr. Jeffrey Evanseck has received the prestigious Presidential Award for Excellence in Research for his scientific and academic contributions, along with his outstanding dedication and leadership in the field of theoretical organic and biophysical chemistry “Dr. Evanseck's 20-year journey in Duquesne’s department of chemistry and biochemistry has been remarkable,” said Dr. Ellen Gawalt, dean of the School of Science and Engineering. “His collaborative spirit has pioneered theoretical and computational research that has unraveled mysteries of natural phenomena and predicted outcomes shaping…
